What part does the Ocean County Clerk play in your sale?

The clerk records your deed. The Ocean County Clerk is a constitutional officer who supervises the filing and recording of every document affecting real estate ownership or transfer in the county. The same office also handles passports and county elections.

For a seller, timing matters here. The land record changes once the clerk accepts the deed, and the state's transfer fee is collected at that step. Send the deed to the office with every required form attached so the filing is accepted on the first visit.

Where are the Ocean County Clerk's offices?

The courthouse at 118 Washington Street in Toms River houses the main office, and three more service points serve other parts of the county. The hours below come from the clerk's contact page.

Ocean County Clerk locations, from the clerk's own website
OfficeAddressPhoneHours
Main office, Courthouse118 Washington Street, Toms River(732) 929-2018Monday to Friday, 8 to 4:30, counter service until 4
Northern Ocean County225 4th Street, Room 211, Lakewood(732) 370-8850Monday to Friday, 8 to 4:30, counter service until 4
County Connection1201 Hooper Avenue, Toms River (Ocean County Mall, near JCPenney)(732) 288-7777Open daily, regular mall hours
Southern Service Center179 South Main Street, Room 106, Manahawkin(609) 597-1500Mon and Fri 8 am to 4:30 pm; Tue to Thu 8 am to 8 pm; in-person service until 4 pm on Mon and Fri

The Manahawkin office stays open until 8 pm on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday, which suits a seller who cannot leave work during the day. The clerk's site also warns that the courthouse, north and south offices close for certain holidays, so call before a trip with a deed in hand.

What does a deed need before the clerk will record it?

It must reach the clerk serving the land's own county, with the transfer fee paperwork attached. The Division of Taxation says a deed recorded in the wrong county has to be recorded again in the correct one, the State fee refunded on Form RTF-3, and the county share of the fee reclaimed from the wrong county's recording office.

  • The deed states the full consideration, because the realty transfer fee is figured on it.
  • Form RTF-1, the Affidavit of Consideration for Use by Seller, goes with any deed that claims a full or partial exemption.
  • A deed on a house with new construction must print the words NEW CONSTRUCTION at the top of the first page and carry an affidavit.
  • A deed over $1,000,000 carries Form RTF-1EE for the percent fee.

Ask the clerk's office for the current county recording charges for your document, since those sit on top of the state fee and the clerk sets the schedule.

How much transfer fee will an Ocean County seller owe?

The fee is figured per $500 of price in brackets. For a price at or below $350,000, the rates are $2.00 per $500 to $150,000, $3.35 per $500 from $150,000 to $200,000, and $3.90 per $500 above that. Above $350,000 the schedule starts at $2.90 per $500 and reaches $4.80 per $500 between $200,000 and $550,000.

The Census figure for a typical owned home in the county is $398,400, which puts a typical sale on the higher schedule. A $400,000 sale works out like this: $870 on the first $150,000, $425 on the next $50,000 and $1,920 on the last $200,000, for $3,215. Parent-to-child deeds, deeds from an executor to an heir and deeds recorded within 90 days after a divorce decree are exempt, and a qualifying senior, blind or disabled seller pays a lower partial rate.

What is Ocean County like for a seller?

Ocean County is the largest county in New Jersey by total area, at 914.84 square miles, and nearly a third of that is water. Toms River is the county seat. The county sits on the Atlantic coast as part of the Jersey Shore, and it includes beach towns such as Seaside Heights, Lavallette, Barnegat Light and Beach Haven on Long Beach Island. The Pine Barrens begin inland.

It was formed on February 15, 1850 from part of Monmouth County, and its 2020 census count of 637,229 was 10.5 percent above the 2010 count of 576,567. Growth picked up after the Garden State Parkway opened in 1954, and it has been the fastest-growing county in the state since 2020. Lakewood Township is the most populous municipality, counting 135,158 people in 2020, and Jackson Township covers the most land.

  • Estimated population: 673,746 in mid-2025.
  • Owned homes: 80.7 percent of the 243,843 households counted for 2020 to 2024.
  • Typical household income of $89,863 and gross rent of $1,755.
  • Residents aged 65 and up make up 24.0 percent.
  • Building permits issued during 2025: 2,831.

With four in five households owning, most Ocean County sellers are selling a home they have lived in.

How do Ocean County's towns and roads affect a listing?

The county holds 33 municipalities, from Lakewood Township, estimated at 139,866 residents in 2023, to small shore boroughs. Jackson Township reaches over 100 square miles, and Toms River is the county seat. The highest ground, three unnamed hills of at least 230 feet in Jackson and Plumsted townships, is far from the sea-level bayfront along Barnegat Bay and the Atlantic.

The Garden State Parkway has fed commuter growth since 1954, and NJ Transit buses link Lakewood and Toms River to New York and Newark. The North Jersey Coast Line stops at Bay Head and Point Pleasant Beach in the northern corner. Many retirement communities run their own shuttle buses to shopping centers. Which town the house sits in decides the tax collector you call and the school district that serves it, while the same county clerk records the deed for all 33.

What should an Ocean County seller ask the clerk before closing?

Ask what is already recorded against the property, because liens show up in the clerk's land records, and a tax sale certificate recorded there will have to be paid off at closing. A holder of a tax sale certificate is told to record it in the county clerk's deed room within 90 days of the sale, so an unpaid-tax lien can show up there.

  • Request a property search for open mortgages, judgments and certificates under your name and the prior owners.
  • Confirm which office accepts your deed, whether the courthouse in Toms River or one of the branch locations, and which hours apply on the day you plan to go.
  • If the house passed through an estate, ask your attorney which exemption applies on the deed.
  • Ask whether a prior deed was recorded in the wrong county, since that can need a refund filing.

Ask for a recorded copy of the deed once it is filed, so you hold proof of the transfer.

Frequently asked questions

Which office records a deed in Ocean County?

Start with the Ocean County Clerk, who records deeds and other documents that affect ownership. The courthouse office at 118 Washington Street in Toms River answers at (732) 929-2018.

Who pays the realty transfer fee on an Ocean County sale?

The seller owes it. The Division of Taxation describes the fee as a charge on the seller for recording the deed.

Can I record my deed in a different county by mistake and fix it?

Yes. Record the deed again in the land's true county, file Form RTF-3 for the State's refund, and ask the wrong county's recording office to refund the county share.

Does an estate sale owe the transfer fee?

A deed from an executor or administrator to an heir or devisee named under the will or the intestacy laws is exempt. A sale by the executor to anyone else is not exempt.

How many Ocean County homes are owner-occupied?

About 80.7 percent for 2020 to 2024, out of 243,843 households, according to the Census Bureau. The middle value of an owned home is $398,400.

Hunterdon County, NJ County Clerk: Recording a Deed, Fees and Transfer Tax

Last updated November 14, 2026.

What does the Hunterdon County Clerk do when a house sells?

Every Hunterdon County deed and mortgage passes through the County Clerk, an elected office that calls itself the Keeper of the Records. Staff in the recording division examine each document for form, dates, signatures, acknowledgment and the property's location. Fees and transfer taxes are settled at the counter when the paper is filed. After that the clerk stamps a recording date, enters the document in the permanent index, sends an abstract of the deed to the local assessor, and hands the original back to the owner.

The office is at 71 Main Street in Flemington, and the mailing address is PO Box 2900, Flemington, NJ 08822. Counter service runs on weekdays until half past four, and the main line is (908) 788-1221. The clerk posts a deed fraud warning and accepts e-filing, which lets whoever handles your closing submit the deed electronically.

How much is the realty transfer fee in Hunterdon County?

State law sets the transfer fee, and the clerk takes it at the counter in addition to ordinary recording charges. Each slice of the price carries its own rate, quoted for every $500 or part of $500. The slices below apply when the total price is over $350,000.

Realty transfer fee per $500 of consideration, sales above $350,000
Slice of the sale priceCharge per $500
First $150,000$2.90
$150,000 to $200,000$4.25
$200,000 to $550,000$4.80
$550,000 to $850,000$5.30
$850,000 to $1,000,000$5.80
Every dollar over $1,000,000$6.05

Source: NJ Division of Taxation form RTF-1EE (rev. 7/10/25), posted by the Hunterdon County Clerk.

A sale at $350,000 or less uses lower rates. A residential sale priced over $1,000,000 adds a separate seller charge, the graduated percent fee, equal to 1 percent of the whole price and rising in steps to 3.5 percent past $3,500,000. The clerk's recording page warns that deeds over $1,000,000 received on or after July 1, 2025 can fall under a revised fee. For an exact number, run the price through the transfer fee calculator the clerk links.

Which Hunterdon County deeds are exempt from the transfer fee?

The state form carries a longer exemption list. These entries matter most to families and estates:

  • Consideration under $100.
  • An executor or administrator conveying to a devisee or heir to distribute the estate under a will or intestate succession.
  • Husband and wife, civil union partners, or parent and child.
  • A deed recorded inside 90 days of a divorce decree dissolving the marriage.
  • Paper that only gives or releases security for a debt, or fixes an earlier recorded deed.
  • A conveyance made on a sale for delinquent taxes or assessments.

An exemption has to be explained in detail on the affidavit. A simple exemption symbol is not enough.

The clerk will not record a deed unless it recites the consideration or carries an affidavit that states it. Consideration includes the money paid, the value of anything else given, and the balance of any mortgage the buyer assumes. Falsifying it is a fourth-degree crime under the state form's warning.

What do Hunterdon County's property tax rates look like?

Because the clerk forwards each deed to the municipal assessor, recording feeds directly into the tax roll. Hunterdon has 26 municipalities, and the state's 2025 table shows effective tax rates running from 1.782 in East Amwell to 3.483 in Hampton. Flemington, the county seat, is at a general rate of 2.736 and an effective rate of 2.984. Lambertville is at 1.902 effective, Clinton Town at 2.808 and High Bridge at 3.152.

The effective rate puts every town on the same footing, so a low general rate does not by itself mean a low bill. Bethlehem Township shows a general rate of 2.021 and an effective rate of 2.350, while Milford shows 4.027 general and 2.944 effective. Look up your own municipality before you choose a list price.

Source: NJ Division of Taxation, 2025 General Tax Rates.

What is Hunterdon County like for a seller?

Western New Jersey holds Hunterdon, a county of 427.84 square miles of land and roughly 301 residents on each. The 2025 estimate is 131,781 residents, and 50,860 households live there. Owners occupy 85.1 percent of the homes, those homes are valued at a median $517,200, and a typical household earns $141,715. Gross rent in the middle of the range is $1,687. People 65 and older account for 23.4 percent of residents, and builders pulled 544 permits in 2025.

Two landscapes divide the county: the Highlands across the western third, and the Piedmont, with the Hunterdon Plateau and Raritan Valley Lowlands, over the rest. Burlington County gave up the land that became Hunterdon in 1714, and the courthouse stands in Flemington. NJ Transit's Raritan Valley Line serves High Bridge, Annandale, Lebanon and Whitehouse Station, and the county LINK offers demand-response service with fixed routes in Flemington. The average commute is 33 minutes.

Source: Census Bureau QuickFacts; Hunterdon County, New Jersey.

How do roads and weather shape Hunterdon house sales?

Hunterdon has about 1,412 miles of public roads, and most of them, roughly 1,059 miles, are kept up by the municipalities. The county maintains about 238 miles and the state about 115, so the road at your driveway may belong to the town, the county or the state. Ask which before you answer a buyer. Trans-Bridge Lines runs buses from Clinton, Flemington, Lambertville and Frenchtown toward Midtown Manhattan and points in Pennsylvania.

In recent years Flemington has seen January lows near 19 degrees and July highs near 85, with precipitation peaking in July. Hunterdon also harvests more deer each year than any other New Jersey county, according to state records, which draws hunters and rural buyers.

Source: Hunterdon County, New Jersey.

How can a seller search Hunterdon County land records?

The clerk's records go back to 1785, and the Record Room is open to the public on weekdays. Help from the Search Room staff is available by appointment at (908) 788-1380. Older records are being redacted to protect identities, with an online system planned after that work ends.

Sellers use these records to confirm the vesting deed, find an open mortgage that needs a release, or locate a recorded lien before a closing. The clerk's recording page also links a homeowner's guide to good deeds, a document reference manual and mortgage foreclosure help for owners behind on payments.

Hunterdon County does not take part in the Homeless Trust Fund, a point the clerk's recording page notes for anyone budgeting fees.

What should I confirm with the clerk before closing?

  • The current recording fee schedule, since only the transfer fee rates are reproduced here.
  • Whether the deed needs the seller's Affidavit of Consideration, required above $1,000,000 or when an exemption is claimed.
  • Who signs the affidavit: the form allows a grantor, a legal representative, or a title or lending officer.
  • How to deliver the package: at the counter, by mail or electronically.
  • The block and lot number, which the form requires and the municipal assessor can supply.
  • Whether the title company or attorney already holds the vesting deed, so the new deed's description matches it.

Frequently asked questions

Where does a Hunterdon County deed get recorded?

In the County Clerk's recording section on Main Street in Flemington. Call (908) 788-1221 before you go, since the office keeps weekday hours only.

Who pays the realty transfer fee on a Hunterdon County sale?

Sellers do. The recorder's block on the state form is labeled as paid by the seller, and the fee arrives at the counter with the deed.

Is a deed from an estate to an heir exempt from the transfer fee?

Yes, when the executor or administrator is carrying out a will or the intestacy laws. That case is listed among the form's exemptions.

Which Hunterdon County town has the highest effective tax rate?

Hampton leads the state's 2025 table at 3.483, while East Amwell sits at the bottom with 1.782.

Can I look up old Hunterdon County deeds?

Yes. Recorded instruments run from 1785 forward, and the public can visit the Record Room and the Search Room on weekdays.

Where do you record a deed for a house in Warren County?

At the Warren County Clerk's Office, inside the Warren County Courthouse at 413 Second Street in Belvidere. The office takes every document that affects ownership or transfer of residential, commercial and industrial property in the county, and it accepts them in person, by mail or electronically.

  • Main office: 908-475-6211.
  • Records room: 908-475-6011.
  • Public records inquiries: 908-475-6220.
  • Fax: 908-475-6208.

Hours are 8:00 am to 4:30 pm on weekdays, and the clerk's contact page asks visitors to call ahead and book an appointment so staff can serve each person efficiently. A seller whose closing is set for a late afternoon should have the title company confirm the recording method in advance.

Recorded documents become public records. Anyone may copy or research them during normal business hours, which is how buyers, lenders and title searchers confirm who owns a parcel and what liens or mortgages are attached. If you need proof of what was filed, a certified copy costs $5 and ordinary copies are $2 a page, with a print from the clerk's website at five cents a page.

What kind of county is Warren County for a seller?

A large county on the Pennsylvania line. Warren County sits in northwestern New Jersey along the Delaware River, across from Easton, Pennsylvania, and it was carved out of Sussex County in 1824. Belvidere is the county seat. Phillipsburg is the most populous of its 22 municipalities, with 15,249 residents in 2020, while Hardwick Township has the most land area and the fewest people.

The county covers 356.54 square miles of land and held about 307 people per square mile in 2020, with the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate at 112,953 residents. Hackettstown has the county's only NJ Transit rail stop, and the mean trip to work is 34.0 minutes.

Housing here leans toward owners: about 75% of homes are lived in by the people who own them.

What does the Warren County Clerk charge to record a deed?

A deed costs $40 for the first page and $10 for each additional page, plus a $10 tax abstract that applies to some documents such as deeds, court orders and easements. The charges below come from the clerk's posted State of New Jersey fee schedule.

Selected Warren County Clerk recording charges, from the clerk's posted fee schedule
ItemCharge
Deed, first page$40
Deed, each additional page$10
Mortgage, first page$30
Mortgage assignment, discharge, release or postponement, first page$40
Cancellation of mortgage$20
Data recording page, paper documents$10 (or $20 if missing)
Each name after the first five$6
Inheritance tax waiver$15
Certified copy$5
Copy of any document$2 per page

The schedule adds that the county charges nothing toward the homeless fund, and that a veteran's DD-214 filing is free of charge.

What is the Data Recording Page, and who needs it?

It is a form the clerk requires for indexing the land record, and paper recordings without it carry a $20 indexing charge instead of the $10 fee. The clerk's recording services page says all land recordings filed on paper, and electronically recorded deeds, must include it.

For documents sent through e-file, the page is required for deeds only. Your title company or attorney normally prepares it with the deed, but if you are handling a family transfer yourself, download the form from the clerk's website and attach it to the first sheet. A missing page is an avoidable $10 surcharge and a possible delay.

What state fee applies when a Warren County deed is recorded?

The New Jersey Realty Transfer Fee, which is collected on top of the clerk's recording charges. The state sets it by the consideration stated in the deed, and the Division of Taxation's own FAQ gives two worked amounts: $1,910 for a $325,000 deed with no exemption, and $475 for a $280,000 deed where the seller qualifies for the senior citizen partial exemption.

  • An Affidavit of Consideration (RTF-1) must be filed with any deed that claims a full or partial exemption.
  • The state lists 16 reasons for a full exemption, and partial exemptions exist for seniors, blind or disabled owners, low and moderate income housing and new construction.
  • A deed recorded in the wrong county must be re-recorded in the county where the land sits, with a refund application to the State on Form RTF-3.

Send the deed to Belvidere only when the land lies in Warren County.

How can you search Warren County land records?

Use the clerk's online public land records search. Choose the guest option and run a search by name to see every recorded document linked to that person, or narrow it to a specific instrument. Major subdivision maps are searchable by municipality, and a full-size map print costs $9 a sheet.

The Computer Access service in the clerk's vault lets visitors look up mortgages, deeds, liens, trade names, inheritance tax waivers, building contracts and maps on terminals. Law firms and title agents that record often can open a charge account with the clerk for recording, certified copies and map copies. Those charge accounts are separate from the accounts set up with the website vendor, which exist only to print copies from the site.

How do Warren County housing numbers look in the Census?

Owners dominate. The Census Bureau's 2020-2024 figures for the county are below.

  • Share of homes occupied by owners: 75.1%.
  • Typical value of an owned home: $346,500.
  • Median household income: $100,869.
  • Median gross rent: $1,409.
  • Households: 45,391, with 2.40 people per household.
  • Residents 65 or older: 21.6%.

A median home value of $346,500 sits just under the $350,000 line the state uses to set its Realty Transfer Fee rates, so many local sales fall close to that dividing line.

What shapes housing and land records across Warren County?

Rivers, farmland and the highway grid. The Delaware River forms the western edge, the Pequest River drains the middle of the county and joins the Delaware at Belvidere, and the Musconetcong is a third river. Most of the county lies inside the Warren Hills viticultural area, home to five active wineries.

Road access runs on U.S. Route 22 near Phillipsburg, U.S. Route 46 and state routes 94, 173, 182 and 122, and Lehigh Valley International Airport in Allentown serves the county by air. A deed that runs past one page adds $10 for each extra sheet, so ask your title company to count pages before you budget the recording cost.

The clerk's office also handles notary oaths, trade names and certificates for documents going out of state, so a seller who needs a clerk's certificate can arrange it at the same visit, at $5 per certificate under the posted schedule.

Frequently asked questions

What is the address of the Warren County Clerk's Office?

413 Second Street, Belvidere, NJ 07823, in the Warren County Courthouse. The main number is 908-475-6211, and the office is open weekdays from 8:00 am to 4:30 pm. Call ahead for an appointment.

What will a Warren County deed filing set me back?

The deed charge is $40 for the first page and $10 for each added page, with a $10 tax abstract on some documents. Add the state Realty Transfer Fee, which depends on the stated consideration.

Can a deed be recorded electronically in Warren County?

Yes. The clerk records documents in person, by mail or electronically. For e-filed documents the Data Recording Page is required for deeds only.

What happens if I leave out the Data Recording Page?

Paper documents without it are charged $20 for indexing, against $10 when the page is attached. Electronically recorded deeds also need the page or the same charge applies.

Is there a fee for filing a veteran's discharge in Warren County?

No. The clerk's fee schedule lists the DD-214 filing as no charge, along with a veteran's ID card and a peddler's license.
